q: Heat is the amount of energy transferred from one object to another because of a difference in _____.
e: Heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference. Heat is the amount of energy transferred from one object to another because of a difference in temperature. Mass or volume is not this quantity.

q: The unit of heat is _____ in SI unit.
e: Heat is energy, so the SI unit is the joule. The unit of heat is joule (J) in SI unit. Calorie (cal) or watt (w) is not this quantity.

q: The heat unit in the CGS system is _____.
e: CGS still uses the calorie for heat. The heat unit in the CGS system is calorie (cal). Do not trade calorie (cal) for kilocalorie (kcal) or British thermal unit (Btu).

q: The heat unit in the MKS system is _____.
e: One kilocalorie raises 1 kg of water by 1 K. That is the MKS heat unit. The heat unit in the MKS system is kilocalorie (kcal). Joule (j) or calorie (cal) is not this quantity.

q: The heat unit in the British system is the _____.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. The heat unit in the British system is the British thermal unit (Btu). Do not trade British thermal unit (Btu) for foot-pound (ft-lb) or kilocalorie (kcal).

q: Heat required to change the temperature of 1 kilogram mass of water by 1 kelvin is called 1 _____.
e: One kilocalorie raises 1 kg of water by 1 K. That is the MKS heat unit. Heat required to change the temperature of 1 kilogram mass of water by 1 kelvin is called 1 kilocalorie. Do not trade kilocalorie for calorie or joule.

q: The German doctor, Robert Mayer, found first that the energy which represents 1 cal is _____ J.
e: Mayer's mechanical equivalent of heat is 1 cal = 4.184 J. The German doctor, Robert Mayer, found first that the energy which represents 1 cal is 4.184 J. 1.356 or 1055 is not this quantity. 4.184 is what this sentence is naming.

q: The relation between heat units is 1 kcal = _____ J.
e: 1 kcal = 4184 J, 1 Btu = 1055 J, and 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J. The relation between heat units is 1 kcal = 4184 J. 1055 or 1.356 is not this quantity. 4184 is what this sentence is naming.

q: The relation between heat units is 1 Btu = _____ J.
e: 1 kcal = 4184 J, 1 Btu = 1055 J, and 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J. The relation between heat units is 1 Btu = 1055 J. Do not trade 1055 for 4184 or 1.356. 1055 is what this sentence is naming.

q: The relation between heat units is 1 ft-lb = _____ J.
e: 1 kcal = 4184 J, 1 Btu = 1055 J, and 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J. The relation between heat units is 1 ft-lb = 1.356 J. Do not trade 1.356 for 4.184 or 1055. 1.356 is what this sentence is naming.
